We have bonded titles here.  
  
 A Texas motorcycle bonded title (Certificate of Title Surety Bond) allows you to register and legally own a motorcycle lacking a proper title. It requires being a Texas resident, having possession of the bike, obtaining a $15 TxDMV "Statement of Fact" (Form VTR-130-SOF), purchasing a surety bond (usually  
  
  
 or less), and paying registration fees, generally totaling  
  
  
 times the bike's value.   
  
 Reddit +5  
**Key Steps for a Texas Bonded Title:**  

1.   **Verify Eligibility:** The motorcycle must not be reported stolen, junked, or in a lawsuit.
2.   **Obtain VIN Inspection:** Get a Form VTR-68-A from a certified inspector (often police) to verify the VIN.
3.       *   **Request a Tax Office Statement:** Visit your local county tax office to get a "Statement of Fact" (Form VTR-130-SOF) and have them determine the value of the motorcycle.
    *   **Purchase Surety Bond:** Buy a bond from a surety company for 1.5 times the value of the motorcycle (minimum $100 for the bond).
    *   **Submit Paperwork:** Submit the VTR-130-SOF, bond, 68-A, and a $15 fee to the TxDMV.
    *   **Register the Bike:** Once the bonded title arrives, register the motorcycle at your local tax office within 30 days.   

**Important Information:**  

*   **Duration:** The bond remains active for three years, protecting against prior ownership claims.
*   **Finalizing:** After three years, the bonded title can be replaced with a standard, clean title.

I still have factory exhaust on mine, although I did do what I call a "stage 1.5" debaffling." I drilled 1 half inch hole into the outer baffles in behind the riveted on plates on my pipes, then reinstalled those plates and it did make it slightly louder, but didn't change the pitch of the exhaust note at all like I had hoped it would. I don't really want to spend the money on aftermarket pipes because from what I have seen they're just straight pipes that make the bike obnoxiously loud, which I don't want. When I last rode in 1975, I rode a [Honda](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-8417659f46-k&k=Honda+motorcycles&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) CB250-K4 (1972 model), then gave up motorcycling for 42 years before returning. In 2017 I got my license then rented an M50, drove it for most of a day. I really enjoyed that bike. Since my first bike was a 250, this was my first experience on a larger (medium sized) bike. I did fine with it, so went shopping for a similar sized bike. For a while I was torn between the C50T and the [Vulcan 900](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C6TG5HHS?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-1f7835cd81-d&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&linkCode=osi&th=1&psc=1&rel=nofollow) Classis LT (I wanted a classic looking light touring model). In many ways the bikes are very similar, but there are differences. The Suzuki has a smaller engine and makes slightly more horsepower. However, the [Vulcan](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-4e8ff5bd7f-k&k=Kawasaki+Vulcan&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) has more torque. Both have similar suspension travel (slightly less front travel for the C50). I wanted good suspension travel for a comfortable ride. Both have low maintenance drives, as I didn't want to mess with a chain drive. The belt drive is more efficient at transferring power than the shaft drive. On a bike with a larger engine the shaft drive would be ideal, but I thought the belt would work better in this power range. I've never ridden a [Honda Shadow](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-68fdbb5ee1-k&k=honda+shadow&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) but would love to know how the shaft drive affects that bike with a 750cc engine. In the end, it was mainly the Suzuki's rear drum brake that decided it for me. I wanted to do the mainenance myself as much as possible, and I thought disc brakes would be easier that a drum brake. We have bonded titles here.  
  
 A Texas motorcycle bonded title (Certificate of Title Surety Bond) allows you to register and legally own a motorcycle lacking a proper title. It requires being a Texas resident, having possession of the bike, obtaining a $15 TxDMV "Statement of Fact" (Form VTR-130-SOF), purchasing a surety bond (usually  
  
  
 or less), and paying registration fees, generally totaling  
  
  
 times the bike's value.   
  
 Reddit +5  
**Key Steps for a Texas Bonded Title:**  

1.   **Verify Eligibility:** The motorcycle must not be reported stolen, junked, or in a lawsuit.
2.   **Obtain VIN Inspection:** Get a Form VTR-68-A from a certified inspector (often police) to verify the VIN.
3.       *   **Request a Tax Office Statement:** Visit your local county tax office to get a "Statement of Fact" (Form VTR-130-SOF) and have them determine the value of the motorcycle.
    *   **Purchase Surety Bond:** Buy a bond from a surety company for 1.5 times the value of the motorcycle (minimum $100 for the bond).
    *   **Submit Paperwork:** Submit the VTR-130-SOF, bond, 68-A, and a $15 fee to the TxDMV.
    *   **Register the Bike:** Once the bonded title arrives, register the motorcycle at your local tax office within 30 days.   

**Important Information:**  

*   **Duration:** The bond remains active for three years, protecting against prior ownership claims.
*   **Finalizing:** After three years, the bonded title can be replaced with a standard, clean title.

When I last rode in 1975, I rode a [Honda](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-8417659f46-k&k=Honda+motorcycles&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) CB250-K4 (1972 model), then gave up motorcycling for 42 years before returning. In 2017 I got my license then rented an M50, drove it for most of a day. I really enjoyed that bike. Since my first bike was a 250, this was my first experience on a larger (medium sized) bike. I did fine with it, so went shopping for a similar sized bike. For a while I was torn between the C50T and the [Vulcan 900](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C6TG5HHS?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-1f7835cd81-d&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&linkCode=osi&th=1&psc=1&rel=nofollow) Classis LT (I wanted a classic looking light touring model). In many ways the bikes are very similar, but there are differences. The Suzuki has a smaller engine and makes slightly more horsepower. However, the [Vulcan](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-4e8ff5bd7f-k&k=Kawasaki+Vulcan&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) has more torque. Both have similar suspension travel (slightly less front travel for the C50). I wanted good suspension travel for a comfortable ride. Both have low maintenance drives, as I didn't want to mess with a chain drive. The belt drive is more efficient at transferring power than the shaft drive. On a bike with a larger engine the shaft drive would be ideal, but I thought the belt would work better in this power range. I've never ridden a [Honda Shadow](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-68fdbb5ee1-k&k=honda+shadow&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) but would love to know how the shaft drive affects that bike with a 750cc engine. In the end, it was mainly the Suzuki's rear drum brake that decided it for me. I wanted to do the mainenance myself as much as possible, and I thought disc brakes would be easier that a drum brake. I also thought that since [Kawasaki](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-e697c5113c-b&k=Kawasaki&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) is more perfromance oriented, I reasoned they thought the bike's design thru a bit better thatn either [Honda](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-8417659f46-k&k=Honda+motorcycles&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) or Suzuki. The [Vulcan](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-287fe9-326854-4e8ff5bd7f-k&k=Kawasaki+Vulcan&tag=vs-pl-vulcanforums-com-20&rel=nofollow) is built like a tank, but this also makes it a bit heavier. On top of that, as the second owner of my bike, it came with the accessories I really wanted, a factory tach, and a Barrons engine guard. The bike was also very stock, which I also wanted.

The bike should provide you exactly what your looking for. Daily rider, weekend cruiser, and a generally easy to maintain bike. With the low mileage, the [tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) will need to be replaced before you ride due to age even though they don't look old. All fluids, rubber hoses, brakes will have to be inspected and or replaced. The mileage suggests it sat for years or was only run a few miles per month. That's bad for anything mechanical. I'm sure it looks in perfect condition... It should. It's not broke in yet. That's problematic. Not a deal breaker in anyway. Just take it to a shop you trust and have it inspected for the items I've mentioned. Old gas, dirty injectors due to sitting will cause it to not run or run badly. The battery may be original and need replacing. Sitting there it's in new condition. The age of components is suspect. Focus on that and you'll realize what it is and you can be confident in the purchase. Pricing will determine whether it's a good deal or not based on what you may have to deal with in the short term to make it a rider. I've got over 72k miles on an 06 model so the bike will last for years and years. I change oil and filter every 3k miles. I've upgrade my front brake hose from rubber to steel. I've changed to a lifetime air filter, clean and replace. I've changed [spark plugs](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-6449d9b0ca-k&k=spark+plugs&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) 3 times. I've changed brake pads 3 times, rear shoes once. [Tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) 4 times. I've had the valves clearance checked and adjusted 4 times.

Welcome to the site - maintenence on the bike is fairly simple and if you are mechanically inclined you can do most of it yourself. If there is no owner's manual, get one online - it will give you the recommended maintenence schedule. Main thing is changing the oil regularly (services the engine and transmission) and keeping an eye on the oil level - these bikes tend to sip some oil. Valves need adjusting about every 7500 miles, other than coolant changes there are no major maintenece items. The bike is a smooth rider till about 65 MPH, then it gets buzzy - that's the main complaint on this bike, the need for a 6th gear. The smaller CC engine runs at a higher RPM than most folks expect for a V-twin so when you are at 4K RPM on the freeway you might feel like the engine is being over worked when it's actually quite happy and has more to give. The two most common add ons for this bike are seats and a replacement final drive called a 'DJ' drive. Do a search within the forum to see what that is. The bike handles nice, if you like the twisties you might find yourself scraping the floorboards - the first time it happend it scared the crap oout of me but I got used to it. It's heavy for a mid cruiser (675-700 lbs) so you will be solid on the freeway.  
  
 As for this bike - ask if the 600 mile maintenece was done - that is key as it sets the tone for the bike mechanically. As others have said, the [tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) need replacing, also pull the final drive off and check the splines for grease - the factory has been known to send these things out dry and the splines get chewed up. Since you indicate you have experience wrenching on bikes, I'll assume you will do an entire maintenence routine if you buy it. After that ride it like you stole it - these are great bikes and I always receommend them.  
  
 Regarding price $3000 - $3500 would be fair based on your description. Low miles on a seven year old bike can actually be a negative as it means the bike most likely sat for extended periods that can be bad for the engine and trany.   
  
 Let us know what happens.

The [C50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) is a great bike. You really get a lot of bang for your buck with the package! Not too heavy, adequate power for freeway travel and light touring, excellent fuel economy and reasonably inexpensive maintenance needs.  
  
 As others have already posted, it starts to get very buzzy at speeds above 65 mph. It is an 800cc Vtwin and that is an awful lot of mass to [sling](https://sling-tv.pxf.io/c/395495/1132376/14334?subId2=fora&adtype=Deeplink) about at 4000+ RPM. You'll feel it in the saddle, floor boards and through the handlebars. Nature of the beast. The one option you have is to install a modified final drive which will help to lower the RPM a bit, but the trade off is a slight drop in available power. Still, if most of your riding is around town or limited to back roads where the speed limit is 55mph or less, you should have no complaints.  
  
 As far as longevity goes, that seems to be a hit or miss proposition. Some people get 60, 70, even 80k miles out of their engine before it needs a major mechanical overhaul. Others aren't so lucky and problems can crop up in as few as 30k miles. It really has nothing to do with anyone's attention to maintenance, it seems to be more luck of the draw.  
  
 With yours being a very low mileage 8 year old bike, I would STRONGLY suggest following the other's suggestions of new rubber, new fluids, etc. Sitting is the enemy for anything mechanical. From the sounds of it, yours has sat a lot.   
  
 I don't know what they are asking for the bike, but I would not pay over $4000

Shields are a personal preference. To be honest though, if you're looking to ride on the slab at over 60mph on a regular basis I'd suggest you look at the [C90](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-5bfa8aca5c-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C90&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) instead. If you don't, you'll be back here complaining about the bike not having a sixth gear and people will tell you to install a [DJ drive](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-7ffaf559aa-k&k=DJ+Drive+C50+final+drive+conversion&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow), which is a modified [C90](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-5bfa8aca5c-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C90&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) drive shaft. Why not skip the middle man and buy the bike with the drive shaft in it. If you're only occasionally going to be riding the slab and you'll spend most of your time on back roads enjoying the scenery and moving through curves the [C50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) is a great bike.

#3·May 8, 2015

The bike should provide you exactly what your looking for. Daily rider, weekend cruiser, and a generally easy to maintain bike. With the low mileage, the [tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) will need to be replaced before you ride due to age even though they don't look old. All fluids, rubber hoses, brakes will have to be inspected and or replaced. The mileage suggests it sat for years or was only run a few miles per month. That's bad for anything mechanical. I'm sure it looks in perfect condition... It should. It's not broke in yet. That's problematic. Not a deal breaker in anyway. Just take it to a shop you trust and have it inspected for the items I've mentioned. Old gas, dirty injectors due to sitting will cause it to not run or run badly. The battery may be original and need replacing. Sitting there it's in new condition. The age of components is suspect. Focus on that and you'll realize what it is and you can be confident in the purchase. Pricing will determine whether it's a good deal or not based on what you may have to deal with in the short term to make it a rider. I've got over 72k miles on an 06 model so the bike will last for years and years. I change oil and filter every 3k miles. I've upgrade my front brake hose from rubber to steel. I've changed to a lifetime air filter, clean and replace. I've changed [spark plugs](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-6449d9b0ca-k&k=spark+plugs&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) 3 times. I've changed brake pads 3 times, rear shoes once. [Tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) 4 times. I've had the valves clearance checked and adjusted 4 times.

Welcome to the site - maintenence on the bike is fairly simple and if you are mechanically inclined you can do most of it yourself. If there is no owner's manual, get one online - it will give you the recommended maintenence schedule. Main thing is changing the oil regularly (services the engine and transmission) and keeping an eye on the oil level - these bikes tend to sip some oil. Valves need adjusting about every 7500 miles, other than coolant changes there are no major maintenece items. The bike is a smooth rider till about 65 MPH, then it gets buzzy - that's the main complaint on this bike, the need for a 6th gear. The smaller CC engine runs at a higher RPM than most folks expect for a V-twin so when you are at 4K RPM on the freeway you might feel like the engine is being over worked when it's actually quite happy and has more to give. The two most common add ons for this bike are seats and a replacement final drive called a 'DJ' drive. Do a search within the forum to see what that is. The bike handles nice, if you like the twisties you might find yourself scraping the floorboards - the first time it happend it scared the crap oout of me but I got used to it. It's heavy for a mid cruiser (675-700 lbs) so you will be solid on the freeway.  
  
 As for this bike - ask if the 600 mile maintenece was done - that is key as it sets the tone for the bike mechanically. As others have said, the [tires](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-04ade51f12-k&k=tires&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) need replacing, also pull the final drive off and check the splines for grease - the factory has been known to send these things out dry and the splines get chewed up. Since you indicate you have experience wrenching on bikes, I'll assume you will do an entire maintenence routine if you buy it. After that ride it like you stole it - these are great bikes and I always receommend them.  
  
 Regarding price $3000 - $3500 would be fair based on your description. Low miles on a seven year old bike can actually be a negative as it means the bike most likely sat for extended periods that can be bad for the engine and trany.   
  
 Let us know what happens.

The [C50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) is a great bike. You really get a lot of bang for your buck with the package! Not too heavy, adequate power for freeway travel and light touring, excellent fuel economy and reasonably inexpensive maintenance needs.  
  
 As others have already posted, it starts to get very buzzy at speeds above 65 mph. It is an 800cc Vtwin and that is an awful lot of mass to [sling](https://sling-tv.pxf.io/c/395495/1132376/14334?subId2=fora&adtype=Deeplink) about at 4000+ RPM. You'll feel it in the saddle, floor boards and through the handlebars. Nature of the beast. The one option you have is to install a modified final drive which will help to lower the RPM a bit, but the trade off is a slight drop in available power. Still, if most of your riding is around town or limited to back roads where the speed limit is 55mph or less, you should have no complaints.  
  
 As far as longevity goes, that seems to be a hit or miss proposition. Some people get 60, 70, even 80k miles out of their engine before it needs a major mechanical overhaul. Others aren't so lucky and problems can crop up in as few as 30k miles. It really has nothing to do with anyone's attention to maintenance, it seems to be more luck of the draw.  
  
 With yours being a very low mileage 8 year old bike, I would STRONGLY suggest following the other's suggestions of new rubber, new fluids, etc. Sitting is the enemy for anything mechanical. From the sounds of it, yours has sat a lot.   
  
 I don't know what they are asking for the bike, but I would not pay over $4000

 I like my 06 [c50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) a lot. I drive it around town all the time, no problems. Our freeway speeds are 70mph and 75mph on parts of a tollway. Because of these high speeds, I opted to switch out the final drive on my [c50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow). Going 75-80 actual mph makes the bike shake, rattle and roll with the original final drive in it. It can go faster, up to and just over 100mph. After the switch, at 75-80mph, I have a nice smooth ride.  
  
 I have no problems taking the bike out for a day of riding. I have no problems staying up with my friends (but they drive their bikes like they borrowed them from their bosses).   
  
 While I haven't had the bike long, about 1 1/2 years and 6k miles, it has run well. I have only had to do regular maintenance and replaced the battery. I have had some issues with a couple of things related to the turn signals from the age of the bike and age of the wires.  
  
 I'm not sure you can get better bang and enjoyment for the money... at least on a motorcycle than the [c50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow).

  
Plan for tomorrow and live for today.​

**Similar Situation**  
  
 I purchased my '08 C50 with just over 4K miles in March of this year for $3900, which is on the high side (as I have learned). But it was the color I was looking for and had been taken very good care of. Lots of great info has been provided, and please take the time to use the search function here as it will provide an incredible amount of pertinent information.  
  
 It took several weeks for me to do all the service that was recommended, but I am kind of slow and double check everything I do (especially when working on the top end). Knowing you need new tires, valve clearance check, oil change, fuel line replacement($50), front brake line replacement, driveshaft spline greasing, antifreeze change, etc, should give you ammunition for price negotiations. I wish I had known all this as I may have saved myself several hundred dollars.... again, maybe not....  
  
 Is it worth it? For me, so far it is! I do have a DJ drive on the workbench to take care of the high speed cruising, and will install it once I start highway cruising. Right now I'm just riding 2 lane backroads.

Shields are a personal preference. To be honest though, if you're looking to ride on the slab at over 60mph on a regular basis I'd suggest you look at the [C90](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-5bfa8aca5c-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C90&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) instead. If you don't, you'll be back here complaining about the bike not having a sixth gear and people will tell you to install a [DJ drive](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-7ffaf559aa-k&k=DJ+Drive+C50+final+drive+conversion&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow), which is a modified [C90](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-5bfa8aca5c-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C90&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) drive shaft. Why not skip the middle man and buy the bike with the drive shaft in it. If you're only occasionally going to be riding the slab and you'll spend most of your time on back roads enjoying the scenery and moving through curves the [C50](https://www.amazon.com/s?ascsubtag=v1-7181ff-348257-e51bf8c623-k&k=Suzuki+Boulevard+C50&tag=vs-pl-volusiariders-com-20&rel=nofollow) is a great bike.

Music, Motorcycles, and Family... Nothing else really matters in life!
